paragraphs.title: Ahithophel's Plan and the Need for Another Opinion

easy.explanation: Ahithophel proposed choosing twelve thousand men.
easy.q: How many men did Ahithophel propose choosing?

easy.explanation: He said, “I will arise and pursue after David this night.”
easy.q: When did Ahithophel propose attacking David?

easy.explanation: Absalom asked them to call Hushai the Archite also.
easy.q: Whom did Absalom ask to hear in addition to Ahithophel?

medium.explanation: Ahithophel planned to smite the king only and then bring the people back.
medium.q: What was Ahithophel's main objective in the attack?

answers: David had a very large army
David and his men were weary and weak
Absalom had already conquered the land
medium.explanation: He expected David to be weary and his followers to flee.
medium.q: Why did Ahithophel think an immediate attack would succeed?

answers: To surprise David while he was weary
To give David time to prepare

challenge.q: What advantage did Ahithophel seek by attacking at night?

answers: He wanted another opinion before deciding
challenge.explanation: Absalom asked to hear Hushai even though Ahithophel's saying pleased him.
challenge.q: What can be learned from Absalom's request to hear Hushai also?

answers: All the people would be killed
The people would remain with David
All the people would be brought back to Absalom in peace

paragraphs.title: Hushai Persuades Absalom to Delay the Attack

answers: As mighty men who were chafed in their minds
easy.explanation: Hushai said that David and his men were mighty and chafed in their minds.
easy.q: How did Hushai describe David and his men?

easy.explanation: Hushai advised gathering all Israel, from Dan to Beer-sheba.
easy.q: What did Hushai advise doing before going to battle?

easy.explanation: Absalom and all the men of Israel said Hushai's counsel was better.
easy.q: Whose counsel pleased Absalom and all Israel?

answers: David and his men were experienced and dangerous warriors
David had already crossed the Jordan
medium.explanation: Hushai emphasized their courage, experience, and determination.
medium.q: Why did Hushai say a quick attack might fail?

answers: A bear robbed of her whelps
medium.explanation: Hushai compared them to “a bear robbed of her whelps in the field.”
medium.q: What image did Hushai use for David and his men?

medium.explanation: The word describes the killing or destruction of many people.
medium.q: What does “a slaughter” mean in this passage?

answers: He warned that an initial defeat could cause fear among Absalom's followers
He said David was not in the camp
He advised attacking only the people
challenge.explanation: Hushai warned that news of an early defeat would cause people to say there was a slaughter among Absalom's followers.
challenge.q: How did Hushai challenge the advantage of focusing only on David?

answers: Ahithophel's good counsel was not followed
challenge.explanation: The decision prevented Ahithophel's proposed plan from being carried out.
challenge.q: What was the immediate result of accepting Hushai's counsel?

answers: Speed and focus versus gathering a large force
Defending a city versus building a temple
challenge.explanation: Ahithophel proposed a quick focused attack, while Hushai urged gathering a huge army.
challenge.q: What central contrast appears between Ahithophel's and Hushai's plans?

paragraphs.title: The Warning Is Sent to David

easy.explanation: Hushai spoke to Zadok and Abiathar the priests.
easy.q: To whom did Hushai report Ahithophel's counsel and his own counsel?

easy.explanation: Hushai told the priests to send word to David.
easy.q: To whom were the priests to send the warning?

easy.explanation: He warned David not to lodge in the plains of the wilderness but to pass over quickly.
easy.q: What did Hushai tell David to do?

answers: He and all the people with him could be swallowed up
He needed to find food in a city
medium.explanation: The warning concerned danger to David and all the people with him.
medium.q: Why was it important for David not to remain in the wilderness?

answers: Absalom's decision made it necessary to warn David and move him quickly
Absalom's decision caused David to return to Jerusalem
medium.explanation: After Absalom accepted Hushai's counsel, David needed to be warned of the danger.
medium.q: What was the connection between Absalom's decision and the warning to David?

medium.explanation: The phrase warns David not to remain in that place during the night.
medium.q: What does “lodge not this night” mean?

answers: They served as a link for sending the message to David
They were supposed to arrest David
challenge.explanation: Hushai gave the information to the priests so they could pass it on to David.
challenge.q: Why were the priests an important part of the plan?

answers: The destruction or capture of David and his people
The loss of their way only
challenge.explanation: The message warned of severe danger to David and everyone with him.
challenge.q: What danger is suggested by “lest the king be swallowed up”?

answers: Hushai reports to the priests, and the priests warn David
David reports to Hushai, and Hushai crosses Jordan
Absalom warns David, and the priests gather an army
challenge.explanation: This is the order described in these verses.
challenge.q: What is the correct sequence of events?

paragraphs.title: The Messengers and the Rescue at the Well

easy.explanation: Jonathan and Ahimaaz stayed by En-rogel and received the message.
easy.q: Who received the message near En-rogel?

easy.explanation: They went down to a well in the court of a man's house in Bahurim.
easy.q: Where did Jonathan and Ahimaaz hide?

answers: She spread a covering over it and put ground corn on it
She built a wall around it
easy.explanation: She covered the well's mouth and spread ground corn over it.
easy.q: What did the woman do to conceal the well?

answers: A lad saw them and told Absalom
medium.explanation: A lad saw them and reported them to Absalom.
medium.q: Why did the messengers have to hide?

answers: She said the messengers had gone over the brook of water
She said they were in Jerusalem
She said they had gone to battle
medium.explanation: She told the servants, “They be gone over the brook of water.”
medium.q: How did the woman mislead Absalom's servants?

answers: They came up from the well and told David
They stayed in the well until morning
medium.explanation: After the servants departed, they came out and reported to David.
medium.q: What did the messengers do after Absalom's servants left?

answers: She protected the messengers and allowed them to continue
She delivered the message to Absalom
She stopped the crossing of Jordan
challenge.explanation: By hiding the messengers and misleading the servants, she helped save them.
challenge.q: What role did the woman play in sending the warning to David?

answers: Delay could have endangered David and his people
The message was only for future planning
challenge.explanation: The messengers urged David to arise and pass quickly over the water.
challenge.q: What does the rapid movement of the message show about time?

answers: David and all the people crossed Jordan by morning
challenge.explanation: David and all the people with him crossed Jordan, and none was left behind.
challenge.q: What happened after David received the warning?

Absalom made Amasa captain of the host instead of Joab.

Absalom sent him on a mission

The war caused Absalom to feed David
